text:
mike: Heads-up — we're seeing ~0.8% of prod traffic end up on the fallback route this morning. Root cause looks like the mobile SDK is sending X-Route: custA but without the signed-assertion header, so the gateway rejects it and falls back to default-model. Anyone else seeing mismatched header precedence?

anya: Confirmed. Mobile change landed last week that strips some headers on Android 13. We only noticed because Dedicated telemetry started nudging up.

cheng: Oof. Current routing rules in the gateway are: prefer signed-assertion, then X-Route, then User-Agent heuristics. If signed-assertion missing => verify X-Route against allowlist. If no match => fallback.

mike: Right. Problem is the X-Route allowlist is permissive for hosted customers to make onboarding easy. That makes spoofing possible if clients can set arbitrary X- headers. We should not rely on X-Route alone for Dedicated routing.

sara: Agreed. For Dedicated tenants we should require either a gateway-signed token (set by edge after authentication) or a signed-assertion header. Otherwise treat X-Route as advisory only.

cheng: Proposed precedence update: signed-assertion > gateway-signed-route (edge signs a canonical X-Route-Sig) > X-Route allowlist > UA. That keeps UA as last resort for legacy proxies.

anya: Telemetry note: we currently only log "route" as the final selected route, but we don't record the decision signal (which header matched or why fallback happened). Need a route_decision tag (values: signed, signed-edge, xroute-allowlist, ua-heuristic, fallback).

mike: +1. Also we need a rate metric for fallback events per-tenant so we can alert if a dedicated tenant loses capacity and starts sending to hosted fallback. Something like metrics: route.fallback.count{tenant,reason}.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: gateway-routing-precedence-update -> staging (canary 0.5%)

mike: UX question for Console: when we roll this change, we should show a banner on the tenant Routing page that explains the new precedence and whether the tenant has a gateway-signed-route enabled. People will ask why their X-Route isn't honored.

sara: Console should also expose a small simulator: paste headers -> shows which policy path would be taken. That avoids cross-team emails.

anya: Security concern: if we add gateway-signed-route we need to ensure it's bound to the upstream auth context (tenant id + request nonce) and rotated keys. Also TTL small (1m) so stolen headers are less useful.

cheng: Implementation notes: config snippet for matching:
```yaml
routing_rules:
  - name: signed_assertion
    match: headers.signed_assertion.exists == true
  - name: gateway_signed
    match: headers.x-route-sig matches "^sigv1:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$"
  - name: xroute_allowlist
    match: headers.x-route matches "^cust-[A-Za-z0-9]+$"
  - name: ua_heuristic
    match: headers.user-agent contains "Redwood-Client"
```
We should inject a route_decision header at the gateway before routing to runtime.
\nmike: Telemetry + alerting plan: add metric route.decision.count by reason. Create alert if fallback ratio > 0.5% over 5m for any tenant with dedicated capacity. Also track quota consumption on fallback: quota.fallback.tokens_used.{tenant}.

ops-bot: noted. Pager policy: if fallback ratio > 5% for >10m escalate to oncall.

anya: Rollout plan: enable gateway-signed-route verification in staging, run a 0.5% canary for 24h in prod (deploy-bot already queued), collect route_decision metrics. After 24h, increase to 5% if no regressions.

cheng: I'll add a small telemetry event in the request trace: decision_reason and matched_header_value (masked) so we can debug misroutes without PII.

mike: Action items: 1) cheng - implement precedence + route_decision header + masked trace fields. 2) anya - add console banner + header simulator UX. 3) sara - spec gateway-signed-route signing + key rotation. 4) ops - add fallback and quota alerts. 5) I will own the canary and review metrics after 24h.

sara: Thanks. One more: we should update docs and the onboarding checklist for customers that use X-Route to recommend enabling edge-route signing for Dedicated.

mike: Cool. If no objections I'll merge the staging change this afternoon and kick the canary. :thumbsup:

anya: No objections from me.

cheng: LGTM.

deploy-bot: deployed gateway-routing-precedence-update to staging at 2102467920

mike: I'll monitor the first canary batch. Will post metrics in this thread in ~2h.
